lightPrompt:
Use case: diagram.
Asset type: OPDA homepage method-loop LIGHT-MODE raster illustration, already an image on a website. Create one polished publication-quality image at exactly 2752×1216 pixels, aspect ratio 43:19 (approximately 2.26316:1). High-resolution lettering and crisp illustration detail; preserve this unusual exact canvas rather than substituting 16:9 or 3:1.
Primary request: redraw a five-node human-governed modelling process with restrained OPDA editorial watercolour vignettes supporting very clear professionally set text. The process is specification and domain modelling, not operating a SaaS. Keep five distinct nodes and exactly five arrows; do not invent stages, agents, data formats, approvals or operational claims.
Layout: a wide horizontal arrangement with Source material at far left, Prepare candidate at centre-left, Working-group review at centre-right, and Draft standard at far right, these four nodes vertically centred near y=610. Publish candidate sits lower, between Prepare and Review, centred near x=1376,y=980. The three middle nodes form a revision cycle: Prepare candidate → Publish candidate → Working-group review → Prepare candidate. The review-to-prepare return travels across the wide empty top area and is labelled Changes requested. Source material enters Prepare candidate once through a horizontal right-pointing arrow labelled Initial intake. Working-group review has a separate horizontal right-pointing gold arrow to Draft standard labelled Consensus reached. Arrowheads must clearly point at the named destination. No reverse arrows, no return to Source material, no shortcut from Prepare directly to Review, no arrow from Draft back into the cycle. The curved return and lower cycle connectors must be individually traceable without overlapping nodes, text or each other. Keep every part of the five nodes and every arrow inside the canvas with at least 36 pixels breathing room.
Visual hierarchy: elegant fine deep-purple organic ink outlines around modest rectangular node areas, very gently rounded corners. One small restrained watercolour vignette at the top inside each node, followed by large very legible sans-serif heading and smaller clear sans-serif body text. Source vignette: a teal evidence folio and a few ivory sheets. Prepare vignette: violet pencil and a small partly assembled card study, no robot or screen. Publish vignette: an open petrol-teal portfolio on a low display support, coral amendment sheet. Review vignette: two adults thoughtfully discussing a sheet, simple natural half-length ink silhouettes, human judgement central. Draft vignette: a thin ivory manuscript with gold stitching, no certificate seal, checkmark or approval stamp. Vignettes must stay secondary to words and must not touch the arrows. This is one coherent editorial watercolour-and-ink treatment, not a mix of photorealistic assets, UI boxes and cartoons.
Text: reproduce exactly the following, without quotation marks. Node 1 heading: Source material. Body: Authorised evidence enters once. Node 2 heading: Prepare candidate. Body: AI assists extraction and comparison. Node 3, the bottom node, heading: Publish candidate. Body: Sources, changes and open questions stay visible. Node 4 heading: Working-group review. Body: Members challenge, correct and decide. Node 5 heading: Draft standard. Body: Reviewed, but not ratified or adopted. Arrow labels exactly: Initial intake; Changes requested; Consensus reached. No other text, numbers, overall title, footer or caption; those belong to live HTML outside this raster.
Palette: cool off-white #F9F9F9 paper reaching every edge; deep-purple #231F2F crisp readable type and ink; petrol teal #0E8478, blue-violet #6C5BD4 and restrained coral watercolour. Revision-cycle and initial-intake arrows blue-violet. Gold #FEC92B is reserved for the consensus exit and draft emphasis. Text areas remain clean and uncluttered. Tactile pigment only within the small vignettes and restrained arrow washes; no heavy background texture, no beige cast, gradient, drop shadow, glow, neon, ornamental plants, floating icons, logo, watermark, signature, computer UI or JSON/code. Produce the single image only, at the exact requested geometry.
